To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ultrafast-laser-induced gratings in hydrogen-loaded optical fibers exhibit a high-temperature annealing response that is dependent on the grating order.

the annealing behavior of first-order and third-order fiber Bragg gratings written in H2 loaded SMF-28 with low-energy femto-second laser pulses can be described by the same model, and that both devices can be considered as good candidates for the fabrication of high-temperature sensors.

we have developed a new method to fabricate fiber Bragg gratings that are stable up to at least 1000 ° C and that we have shown that these high-temperature stable gratings are regenerated versions of ultrafast laser induced first-order fiber gratings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of high temperature sensors and sensor systems for applications in harsh environments.
the development of fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) that are stable in high temperatures.
the annealing of ultrafast laser-written first- and thirdorder fiber Bragg gratings in hydrogen loaded SMF-28 optical fibers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the first-order gratins can regenerate and the third-order gratins do not.
the third-order grating is the more stable of the two devices.
the third-order gratins are more stable than the first-order ones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the third-order gratins can be used as high-temperature stable gratings, while the first-order gratins can serve as a high-temperature stable sensor.
the annealing of hydrogen loaded fiber gratings can be controlled and optimized to achieve a stable device at high temperatures.
we have demonstrated a new method for fabricating high-temperature stable Bragg gratings in hydrogen-loaded fiber using ultrafast laser pulses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the isothermal and the isochronal response of the gratings are different, which is important for the design of fiber sensors.
the annealing of ultrafast laser-written fiber gratings can be used as a powerful method for tailoring their high-temperature stability.
the annealing response of fiber gratings can be tailored to meet specific application requirements. © 2016 Optical Society of America.
